name: Hans-Rudolf Gerber
bio:
Hans-Rudolf discovered his passion for motorsport early on, spending countless hours tinkering with model cars and poring over technical schematics. This fascination led him to pursue a degree in mechanical engineering, where he specialized in fluid dynamics. After graduating, he joined a small engineering firm that consulted for various racing teams, giving him his first taste of professional motorsport. He joined ART Grand Prix Academy ten years ago and has become a crucial member of the aerodynamics team.

Hans-Rudolf's meticulous approach to data analysis and his ability to identify subtle aerodynamic improvements have earned him a reputation as a highly reliable and effective wind tunnel operator. He prides himself on his ability to translate complex data into actionable insights for the engineers, bridging the gap between simulation and real-world performance. He's always looking for new ways to optimize testing procedures and improve the accuracy of the wind tunnel data.

What sets Hans-Rudolf apart is his uncanny ability to spot anomalies in the wind tunnel data that others often miss. His deep understanding of the underlying physics, combined with his years of experience, allows him to identify potential issues early on, preventing costly mistakes and ensuring that the team is always working with the most accurate information possible.

physical.hairStyle: Short, neatly combed back with a slight wave.
physical.description: A man of medium build, with a focused gaze and a perpetually thoughtful expression.

quirks: Always carries a small notebook filled with hand-drawn diagrams and calculations.
Has a habit of humming quietly while reviewing wind tunnel data.
Insists on wearing his lucky racing socks to every wind tunnel session.
